facts.statement: The genus Abdounia was described by Cappetta in 1980.
Abdounia fossils date from the Danian to the Rupelian stages.
Abdounia fossils have been found in the Paleogene of Morocco, France, Belgium, Russia, and the United States.
facts.quote: Fossil Abdounia teeth are known from the Paleogene of Morocco, France, Belgium, Russia, and the United States (North Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, and Virginia).

facts.statement: In the lower Nanjemoy Formation of Virginia, Abdounia teeth are the most common fossil shark teeth.
facts.quote: In the lower Nanjemoy Formation of Virginia, they are the most common fossil shark tooth.

facts.statement: By the end of the Oligocene, the genus was severely reduced, likely due to competition with other sharks like Carcharhinus.
facts.quote: By the end of the Oligocene Epoch the genus is severely reduced, probably due to competition with other Carcharhiniformes like Carcharhinus.

facts.statement: Abdounia belongs to the family Carcharhinidae.
Abdounia is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Abdounia lived between 66 and 27.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Rupelian (66 to 27.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Abdounia is an extinct genus of requiem shark known primarily from isolated teeth.
rejected.quote: Abdounia is an extinct genus of requiem shark which lived during the Paleogene period, and is mainly known from isolated teeth.
